content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge labels Isaiah 7:14 UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, thereby treating a single verse's two senses as leaving the matter open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"The phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.' has two readings I weighed: it forbids an UNDERDETERMINED label based on Isaiah 7:14's almah/bethulah ambiguity; or it is inapplicable if the judge is instead weighing two chains (chapter bounds versus Matthew 1:23).","why":"The judge's UNDERDETERMINED rests in part on treating Isaiah 7:14's two lexical senses as leaving the question open, which K-S2 says is not open because both senses stand."}
